study.title: Neural Effects of Low-Frequency Acupoint Electrical Stimulation Therapy on Patients With Poststroke Motor Dysfunction: A Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study
study.journal: Archives of Rehabilitation Research and Clinical Translation
study.population: Patients with poststroke motor dysfunction (infarcts in the right basal ganglia region) and age- and gender-matched healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) MRI/CT-confirmed stroke; (2) age 45-75 years, time since stroke onset 7-30 days, right-handedness; (3) first episode, stable condition, no cognitive impairment (Mini-Mental State Examination ≥27) or increased muscle tone (Ashworth grade 0); (4) infarct location in the right basal ganglia region with volume <2.7 cc; (5) unilateral limb dysfunction (Fugl-Meyer Assessment [FMA] <85 points); (6) stable vital signs and ability to tolerate MRI examination; and (7) signed informed consent. Healthy subjects: (1) aged 45-75 years, right-handed; (2) healthy motor function in all limbs; and (3) signed informed consent.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) concurrent traumatic brain injury, tumor, epilepsy, or major organ failure; (2) previous thrombolytic/thrombectomy therapy; (3) absolute contraindications for MRI; (4) infection at stimulation site or intolerance to electrical stimulation; (5) any clinically significant intracranial abnormality other than the acute stroke lesion, as confirmed by fMRI (eg, congenital malformations, space-occupying lesions, cerebrovascular malformations, or prior cerebral infarctions or hemorrhages); and (6) a history of skin allergies or sensitivity to electrode gels, adhesives, or other materials used in the electrical stimulation procedure. Healthy subjects: (1) history of traumatic brain injury or neuropsychiatric disorders; and (2) absolute contraindications for MRI (eg, claustrophobia, intracranial metal implants, and cardiac electronic devices).

arms.dropouts: 2 excluded post-treatment: 1 fMRI terminated (second MRI scan abandoned), 1 excluded during analysis (excessive head motion resulting in poor image quality)

extraction_notes.note: Neuroimaging results (Figures 3 and 4) are presented as brain maps without coordinate tables. No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported for any brain regions. Region labels are taken from figure captions only (e.g., PHG, PreCG, MFG, SFGdor, SMA, Cerebellum, Vermis, ANG, PoCG). Cluster sizes, peak t-statistics, and other table-level data are entirely absent.

Coordinate space is not explicitly stated in the paper. Normalization was performed to 'Montreal Neurological Institute space,' which implies MNI coordinates, but the coordinate space label is not confirmed in any results table.
No adverse events section is present in the paper. Neither safety reporting nor explicit statements about absence of adverse events were found.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding/allocation guessing were not assessed or reported anywhere in the paper.
No quantitative deqi measurement instrument (e.g., MASS, VAS for deqi sensations) was used. Only qualitative mention that 'deqi was achieved' for scalp/head needle insertion.

The paper does not report a sham or placebo control arm. The healthy control group received no treatment and underwent only a single fMRI scan. This limits causal inference about treatment-specific neuroimaging effects.

The paper describes the pulse width for scalp stimulation as '100 ms' but uses the symbol 'ms' in one place and 'μs' in another place in the abstract. In the methods section (page 4/5) it is stated as 'pulse width 100 ms' for head, '200 ms' for upper limb, and '400 ms' for lower limb. In the abstract it uses 'μs'. The units may be inconsistent across abstract and methods. The methods text values were used for extraction.

The correlation for NIHSS is stated as 'r=.435' in the text but the figure caption describes it as 'r=−.435'. The negative correlation direction is explicitly described in the text ('negatively correlated with improved NIHSS scores'). The negative sign was preserved in the neural_results entry.

The paper states 20 HCs were enrolled and analyzed, and 28 Tx patients were analyzed for neuroimaging (total n=48), but clinical outcomes are only reported for the Tx group (n=28). HCs were assessed on FMA, MBI, NIHSS at baseline for screening only, and these scores are not tabulated.

The study design is described as a 'case-control study' but has no randomization or sham group. Clinical improvement in the Tx group cannot be attributed specifically to the intervention without a control comparison group for clinical outcomes.
Supplemental table S1 describing detailed textual descriptions of acupoint locations is referenced but not available in this PDF. Exact textual acupoint location descriptions could not be extracted.

The paper does not report which hemisphere corresponds to 'ipsilateral' vs 'contralateral' in the context of the angular gyrus finding. The angular gyrus decrease is described as 'contralateral angular gyrus' post-treatment, which given right-side basal ganglia infarcts and left-side affected limbs would imply left angular gyrus — consistent with 'left angular gyrus' as labeled in figure caption.
The paper does not report global signal regression status explicitly in the preprocessing pipeline.

The exact number of initial time points discarded ('discarding initial 10 time points') leaves 230 volumes for analysis from the 240 total acquisitions, but the effective scan duration after discarding is not explicitly stated.
